summary:
LFM3-1.7B: 47 of 61 screened parts passed. Every pass targets one of three narrow skills: Roman numerals, month succession or object colour. Nothing passed for the broad built-ins (math, code, multilingual, facts), weekday, comparative adjectives, number words, ordinals or nationality-to-country. I couldn't define new skills because the skill cap was already reached.

**Where the skills live**
- **Roman numerals:** 40 passes, mostly MLP clusters, one at every layer from L4 to L23 except L16. One attention group also passed: L20 heads 3, 7, 10 and 11 (drop .394). It barely beats chance, since two random 4-head sets reached .375 and .312.
- **Months:** MLP clusters at L5, L6, L8, L9, L12–L16 and L19.
- **Object colour:** L19 (64 units) and L16 (20 units).

**Passing parts of 64 units or more (the size wanted for transfer)**

| Skill | Layer | Sizes (units) | Drop |
|---|---|---|---|
| Roman | L18 | 64, 256 | .70 |
| Roman | L19 | 64, 128 | .70 |
| Roman | L17 | 64, 128 | .49 |
| Roman | L13 | 64, 128 | .48–.49 |
| Roman | L10 | 64, 128 | .34–.40 |
| Roman | L8 | 64 | .28 |
| Roman | L9 | 64 | .28 |
| Roman | L15 | 64 | .24 |
| Month | L5 | 64 | .55 |
| Month | L14 | 64, 128, 256 | .45–.49 |
| Month | L15 | 64, 128 | .29–.31 |
| Month | L16 | 64 | .29 |
| Colour | L19 | 64 | .44 |

The weights back up the labels: the L18 lead unit's output projection reads as nothing but Roman numerals, the L19 Roman cluster's reads as III/II/IV/IX, and the L16 month cluster writes month names.

The remaining passes are 20-unit sets with drops of .22–.78: Roman at L4, L6, L7, L8, L10–L15, L17 and L19–L23; month at L5, L6, L8, L9, L12, L13, L16 and L19; colour at L16.

**Method that worked**
1. Run an attribution scan on a single layer, which returns at most 20 units per skill.
2. Grow that set to 64–256 units by picking units whose gate rows and down-projection columns are most similar to the seeds.
3. Ablate, then screen.

Growing kept the parts selective in most layers from L5 to L19. It diluted the effect at L4, L6, L7, L22 and L23. At L9, L12 and L13 the month sets failed held-out once grown to 64.

**What did not work**
- Whole blocks of 1–2 layers always dropped facts and general text by .2–.9.
- Early attention-head groups (L6, L8, L10, L14) broke nearly every skill.
- Picking units by how strongly they write the target tokens, or by activation alone, had almost no effect when ablated.
- Late MLP clusters for code, math, multilingual and geography dropped their targets by under .1.
- Weekday stayed tangled with month at every layer tested.
- The comparative-adjective heads at L20 overlap the Roman heads, and the comparative group did no better than random heads.
